title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD & Roadmap (v20)
author: Daniel Park
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD, high-level design, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line (v20). It is intended for engineers, product managers, sales enablement, and customer success teams to align on scope, requirements, rollout strategy, and commercial framing.

Summary
- Product: Unified Inference (hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
- Goal: Provide a unified developer experience with predictable latency and unit economics across deployment modes while offering strong observability and rollout controls.
- Target customers: AI-native startups, mid-market product teams, enterprise platform teams.

1) Goals and Success Metrics
- Customer-facing goals:
  - Offer a single API & config surface that lets customers switch between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with minimal code changes.
  - Reduce median token latency for 2048-context LLM workloads by 20% compared to v18.
  - Reduce per-token cost by 15% for common production workloads through smarter batching, caching, and quantization suggestions.
- Business metrics:
  - Adoption: 30% increase in customers using more than one deployment mode by EOY.
  - Revenue: 18% uplift in Dedicated contract value from upsells tied to SLA guarantees.
  - Reliability: 99.95% platform availability for Dedicated customers; target P95 tail latency SLOs defined per model family.

2) Scope (In-scope for v20)
- API parity for generation, chat, embeddings, and structured outputs across all deployment modes.
- Model routing & fallback policies (cost-aware routing, regional fallback).
- Redwood Optimize integration: automated batch/cache tuning + quantization recommendations.
- Console additions: per-route cost breakdown, rollout controls (canary/A-B), model-version pinning, quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
- Pricing & packaging: launch tiered pricing for Hosted, Commit tiers for Dedicated, and enterprise pricing for Private with support SLAs.

3) Key Requirements
Functional requirements:
1. API compatibility: existing SDKs and REST endpoints must accept new routing/config parameters without breaking changes.
2. Model routing policy engine: support rule-based and ML-guided policies (latency-first, cost-first, region-preferred).
3. Fallback behavior: automatic fallback to pinned smaller/quantized variant on capacity or degraded perf.
4. Observability: token-level cost attribution, per-model and per-route latency histograms, traceable request IDs into runtime.
5. Rollouts: support canary (5/25/50%), A/B splits, and automated rollback on quality/regression signals.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 targets per model family documented in performance-standards.
- Availability: 99.95% for Dedicated, 99.9% for Hosted API.
- Security: all Private deployments must integrate with customer KMS; audit logs retained per customer contract.
- Scalability: autoscaling must support 5x baseline QPS for burst traffic within 10 minutes.

4) Design & High-level Architecture
High level:
- Control plane (Redwood Console & API): orchestration of deployment configs, routing policies, rollouts, billing attribution.
- Data plane (Serving runtime): optimized GPU runtime with continuous batching, KV-cache, quantization-aware kernels, and model-variant support.
- Routing & policy service: evaluates incoming request against policy store and selects appropriate model variant and region.
- Observability pipeline: traces, metrics, and token-level cost events aggregated into per-customer dashboards.

Config table (example):
| Config key | Type | Default | Description |
| routing.policy | string | latency_first | routing policy (latency_first|cost_first|region_pref) |
| rollout.canary_percent | int | 5 | initial canary percent for new model deployments |
| kv_cache.enabled | bool | true | enable prefix / KV caching per deployment |
| quantization.profile | string | auto | recommended quantization profile (auto|int8|int4|none) |

5) Detailed Design Notes
- Model Variants: each model in catalog must include metadata: family, size, quantization support, token throughput, compatibility tags. This enables automatic fallback mapping between variants.
- Batching strategy: runtime implements adaptive batching windowing tuned by request latency SLO and request size distribution.
- Cache semantics: prefix caching with TTLs per route; cache invalidation hooks when model versions are rolled out.
- Rollout detection: quality regressions detected via evaluation harness tied to customer prompt-sets; threshold breach (e.g., >5% drop in accuracy/score) triggers automatic rollback.

6) Roadmap & Themes (next 4 quarters)
- Q2 2026 (current): API parity, routing engine v1, basic rollback policies, pricing tiers defined.
- Q3 2026: Redwood Optimize integrated into console, automated batch tuning, improved per-token cost attribution.
- Q4 2026: Private on-prem installer improvements, KMS/HSM integrations for Private, additional compliance packaging.
- Q1 2027: Advanced ML-guided routing, predictive autoscaling based on workload forecasts, multi-cloud capability.

Themes: "Performance & Economics", "Predictable Operations", "Enterprise Readiness". Each theme maps to measurable OKRs documented in roadmap tracker.

7) Pricing & Packaging Notes
Principles:
- Clear unit economics and predictable billing for committed capacity.
- Simple host-tier pricing for self-serve; differentiated enterprise packages for Dedicated/Private.

Tiering (proposed):
- Hosted (self-serve): pay-as-you-go per token for generation (prompt+completion) and per-embedding unit; volume discounts at usage thresholds (100M tokens/month, 1B tokens/month).
- Dedicated (committed): monthly/annual reserved capacity pricing with baseline throughput and predictable per-token supplement for burst. Commit tiers: Small (4 GPUs), Medium (16 GPUs), Large (64+ GPUs) with unit discounts.
- Private (enterprise): platform license + deployment fee + optional managed-support SLA. Add-ons: extended observability retention, compliance evidence package, SOC-2-like package for audits.

Migration & uplift pricing guidance:
- Offer 90-day trial credits for Dedicated evaluation.
- Provide migration credits for customers moving >50% traffic from self-serve Hosted to Dedicated within first year.

8) Release Notes (v20.0 launch)
Release date: 2026-03-25
Highlights:
- Unified API parity across deployment modes (generation/chat/embeddings).
- Routing engine v1: latency and cost-aware routing, region-aware fallback.
- Console: per-route cost breakdown, canary rollout controls, model-version pinning.
- Redwood Optimize: initial recommendations for batching and quantization.
- Pricing: new Dedicated commit tiers and Hosted volume discounts.

Migration notes for customers:
1. Review any custom SDK integrations that set private routing fields; ensure compatibility with new routing.policy values.
2. Test canary deployments with 5% traffic before full rollout.
3. For Dedicated customers, sign the updated SLA to receive 99.95% availability guarantees.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: GA release to self-serve Hosted + announcements to existing Dedicated pilots.
- Week 1-4: Invite early adopter Dedicated customers to opt into routing and canary features.
- Week 4-12: Ramp for general Dedicated customers; monitor platform SLOs and cost attribution signals.

Monitoring & KPIs post-release:
- Adoption: number of customers using routing policies, percent using Dedicated commit tiers.
- Performance: median token latency, P95/P99 per model family.
- Cost impact: average per-token cost for top 20 workloads.
- Quality: number of rollback events triggered by regression alerts.

9) Operational Runbook (short)
- Owner: product@redwood.com, runtime-support@redwood.com
- Incident triage: if routing engine degrades (error rate > 1% or 5xx spike), immediately toggle to safe-mode policy (route to stable model variant) and page oncall.
- Rollback: use Console rollout UI to revert canary to 0% and promote last-known-good model.

10) Open questions and next steps
- Pricing: finalize Dedicated commit tier price points with finance & go-to-market by 2026-04-10.
- Routing: evaluate ML-guided routing A/B against rule-based policies in Q3 pilot.
- Compliance: scope additional evidence for Private deployments (EU data residency + automated deletion).
